claims.text: Grain boundaries act as preferential nucleation sites for premelting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Grain boundaries lower the local energy barrier for atomic disorder and melting.
Polycrystalline FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles with a high grain-boundary density will begin their phase transition earlier than single-crystalline counterparts.
Polycrystalline FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will progress through the phase transition more rapidly than single-crystalline counterparts.
High-temperature annealing will produce nearly single-crystalline FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles with minimal grain boundaries.
Rapid quenching will produce polycrystalline FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles with a high grain-boundary density.
Grain-boundary density will be quantified using statistical TEM and EBSD mapping.
The two nanoparticle series will be exposed to identical thermal cycles in inert Ar at a heating rate of approximately 10 K/min.
Structural evolution will be monitored in situ using high-resolution TEM, with EBSD used for grain-boundary tracking.
Abundant grain boundaries in polycrystalline nanoparticles cause premature local disorder.
Premature local disorder at grain boundaries accelerates the overall phase transition.
Polycrystalline nanoparticles will exhibit localized surface disorder at lower temperatures than single-crystalline nanoparticles.
Polycrystalline nanoparticles will exhibit intergranular melting at lower temperatures than single-crystalline nanoparticles.
Single-crystalline, defect-minimized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles heated under otherwise identical conditions constitute the baseline.
The proposed conclusions are restricted to inert Ar, a temperature ramp of approximately 10 K/min, and temperatures approaching the premelting and melting regimes.
Classical defect-mediated theories support a role for grain boundaries in facilitating premelting.
The quantitative effect of grain boundaries on melting onset and transition speed may depend on their distribution, orientation, and character.
DSC measurements will be used to corroborate the phase-transition signatures observed by microscopy.

Failure of polycrystalline nanoparticles to show a statistically significant earlier onset of localized melting or premelting than the single-crystalline control would falsify the proposed dominant role of grain boundaries.

contradictions.description: The design states that grain-boundary density is ensured to be the only significant difference between the annealed and quenched samples, while the uncertainty field concedes that other microstructural variations may influence the thermal response. Annealing and quenching could themselves create such uncontrolled differences.
